sub_scenario.one_line: release operations lead: request an accommodated attendance option

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the handover board and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The on-call calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can spend an ordinary afternoon reviewing release notes without feeling depleted.
So routine desk work is sustainable?
Yes, when it follows a normal night's sleep.
Someone new shadowed me in the release room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the pager rotations into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After Tuesday's overnight pager rotation, I closed the handover board at 10:45 and slept until noon.
How did the afternoon feel?
I could handle essentials, but I had no reserve for a long group event.
I enjoyed a short team lunch after last month's daytime deployment.
Did the social part tire you?
No, because I could leave after an hour.
I archived last cycle's notes on the on-call calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The new pager tone has kept waking me for three weeks, even on quieter nights.
Has that changed your recovery?
I stay foggier after call than I used to.
A vendor call about the handover board ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the release room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the pager rotations.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the on-call calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
My shoulder physiotherapy is booked for Thursday at 17:30, and the clinic has no other appointment this week.
Can you reschedule it?
No, missing it would interrupt the treatment plan.
I sketched next week's plan for the pager rotations before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the handover board updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I avoid coffee after two because it brings back the palpitations I had during the spring release.
Can caffeine extend your afternoon?
No, I protect sleep instead.
I compared two options for the on-call calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the release room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The team wants my answer today for a Thursday 14:00–16:30 offsite after my pager rotation. What should I say?
